claim: R5-03 (§4.11 *The clock* (4) l. 8480-8484; V08 §3.6 (3) l. 1870-1875) applies a held late calamity's F5 targets' dossier events at the absorb that holds it — 'now at `W₀` as element events, finished (no Works)', each target's use closed and its building `ruined` (F5 l. 12205; l. 8588 'present as its ruin') — and lets the calamity strike at the first epoch a later absorb folds, whose `EpochInputs.dossier` carries no F5 record of it (V08 §3.6 (3): the F5 events ride the epoch only 'where `W₁` is after `W₀`'). V06 §3.11.1 (l. 2087-2090) defines 'struck in place' for the reverse order only: 'the hazards phase reads the epoch's dossier events for the F5 records tied to the calamity, and exempts those targets' uses from relocation … and the `dossier` phase's F5 then finds a building already struck, which is idempotent'. Nothing says what the held calamity's strike does to targets already ruined. As written the fire ignites at 'the building there' — the targets' centroid, a ruined target (§3.11.2 (1)) — spreads to any 'unburnt, unprotected neighbour', ruined targets included, and its `burn` sets 'existence → decayed with Works kind decay, stage CHARRED' (V06 §2.8 l. 720): a dossier ruin taken back to `decayed` with a new decay run at the later epoch, against §2.6 step 7's 'the level never falls while the building stays abandoned, decayed or ruined'. Another builder skips ruined buildings, igniting at the nearest live one: the targets never charred, a different struck set and `maxBuildings` count. Two builders, two behaviours on the path R5-03 defines (a calamity recorded in the week of the last sync); no bar runs it (T-V8-49 (g) and T76-1 assert only 'the calamity's strike at its first epoch's first week'; T-V6-27 runs on-time calamities).
required_change: V06 §3.11.1, after '…which is idempotent.' add: 'A calamity held late (`DossierBinding.lateCalamities`; §4.11 *The clock* (4)) rides a later epoch whose dossier events hold no F5 record of it, its targets applied at the absorb that held it, ruined and finished (V08 §3.6 (3)): the hazards phase reads its targets from its `CalamityRef.targets`, places it at their centroid as any calamity, and strikes them by no op — each target building keeps `ruined` (its use already closed, never relocated, never taken back to `decayed`, no Works) while counting as struck: a fire's ignition is the target nearest the place and its spread starts from every target as a burning building, each counted toward `maxBuildings`; a flood's or a quake's struck set and count include them likewise; every other building is struck by the hazard's own rule, and its `deaths` reach that epoch's burial need (V06 §3.18.2).' V06 §3.21's hazards row (l. 3293) adds the input 'a held late calamity whose targets are already ruined' with the outcome 'its targets kept `ruined`, struck by no op, the hazard spreading from them (V06 §3.11.1)'. T-V6-27 adds 'and a calamity held late by a second absorb in the last epoch's own week (V08 T-V8-49 (g)'s case): at the later absorb's first epoch its targets stay `ruined` with no op on them, its fire spreads from them to their live neighbours, and its deaths are in that epoch's burial need'. END under V08: §3.6 (3)'s 'so V06's hazard phase strikes them in place' adds '(a held one's targets, applied at the absorb that held it, struck by no op, V06 §3.11.1)'; T-V8-49 (g)'s 'the calamity's strike at its first epoch's first week' adds ', its targets kept `ruined`'. (If the adjudicator rules the other order instead — a held calamity's F5 events held with it to ride its epoch's `EpochInputs.dossier` at that epoch's first week — §4.11 *The clock* (4), V08 §3.6 (3), §3.17's row and T-V8-49 (g) change in its place, and §5.3's coherence row names the held case, the dossier's ruined records then unmet on the map until that epoch.)

claim: V06 §3.7.2 (1) (l. 1476–1478) opens 'each gate of the ring … → `gateToJunction`' on every ring with a pathway, sparing none. By §4.8 *Gates*, a raised gate is a main gate of the ring, 'a gate whose tower carries the deck, its portal on the raised part only' (l. 7671–7673). §2.7's support step (3) (l. 2556–2565) holds the stretch under a crossing station while the deck stands, and R5-02 says no removal of the wall takes it. Its list of removals that pass over the stretch is: `DeclineOp`'s breach and dismantle, V06 §3.7.7 (2)'s decay, a hand op's dry run, a delete, `wallToWay`, `absorbWall` and the hand-off down. V06 §3.7.6 (5) (l. 1611–1619) spares the stretch from (2)'s dismantling. Neither names (1)'s gate opening, and `gateToJunction` has only its type (§4.11 l. 8197) and `wallToWay`'s 'gates become junctions'. On V06's ordinary pathway a CITY whose S4 viaduct took a raised gate in S3's ring has that ring superseded, and its gates open by chance each year. A builder can make a junction on the deck (against item 110 (f)'s zero junctions), remove the tower carrying the deck (leaving it unsupported), or skip the gate. The outcome is undefined on a normal path. A hand `convert` `gateToJunction` of a raised gate falls only under §2.7 (3)'s generic 'a hand op's dry run bends its stretch round it', and §7.1's `bend.wall.held` row, which lists the held stretch's removals, does not name it.
required_change: V06 §3.7.2 (1): 'Each gate of the ring, from its drawn' → 'Each gate of the ring — but a raised gate, whose portal on the deck joins no ground way and whose tower carries the deck (§2.7's support step (3); V06 §3.7.6 (5)), which is no candidate, the part-0 way's own ground gate beneath it, if any, a candidate as any gate — from its drawn'. V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s last bullet: after 'V06 §3.7.2 (2)'s dismantling never takes the stretch that holds a raised gate whose deck stands', add ', nor (1)'s gate opening the raised gate'. T-V6-47's H-AQUA clauses add 'a superseded ring whose raised gate carries a standing viaduct's deck — its gates opened over the pathway, the raised gate kept with its tower carrying the deck, no junction on the deck'. Second end, model, §2.7's support step (3): 'and `DeclineOp`'s `breach` and `dismantle` and V06 §3.7.7 (2)'s decay pass over it in chain order' → 'and `DeclineOp`'s `breach` and `dismantle`, V06 §3.7.7 (2)'s decay and V06 §3.7.2 (1)'s gate opening (`gateToJunction`, which never takes a raised gate) pass over it in chain order'. Second end, determinism, §7.1's `bend.wall.held` cause: 'a hand `convert` `breach` or `dismantle` of an enceinte stretch' → 'a hand `convert` `breach`, `dismantle` or `gateToJunction` of an enceinte stretch or of its raised gate'.

claim: The amended H-AQUA definition (V06 §7, l. 4063-4074) states the conditions under which 'the founding lays' its viaduct: the valley deeper than `viaduct.minDropM`, and `chance` and `pMax` raised to 1. These are not enough. (a) V06 §3.19 (2) (l. 2776-2777) also requires the span within `viaduct.maxSpanM` and the strength `saved − span × viaduct.spanCostFactor` above 0. With V11's factor of 4, the main approach road's ground course from `A` to `B` must be more than five times `|AB|`. §3.19 (5) also drops a course past `raisedWays.structure.maxPierM` or `maxClearSpanM`. A road crossing its valley nearly straight founds nothing. The repair added `pMax` for this very reason but missed these. (b) T-V6-47 (l. 4170) runs 'a viaduct a later trace meets gets no gate', yet the definition lays the METROPOLIS circuit across the elevated road only. Whether a later trace meets the viaduct (from `A` just inside the CITY ring to `B` beyond the valley) depends on growth the definition does not fix. The elevated road does not stand in for it: the viaduct carries the main approach road, a primary, so it is the case where the gate law must read the crossing on ground part 0 and pin no gate on the deck. This is R5-10's class (a test names a case its fixture need not hold); a build agent tunes the recipe, so nothing built changes.
required_change: V06 §7's H-AQUA definition: '(the recipe's valley deeper than `viaduct.minDropM`, its rim at the ring's foot so that the reading's `A` lies inside the ring, V06 §3.19 (2);' → '(the recipe's valley deeper than `viaduct.minDropM`, its rim at the ring's foot so that the reading's `A` lies inside the ring, the main approach road's ground course from `A` to `B` longer than (1 + `viaduct.spanCostFactor`) × `|AB|` with `|AB|` within `viaduct.maxSpanM` so that the reading's strength is above 0, and its piers and clear spans within `raisedWays.structure.maxPierM` and `maxClearSpanM`, V06 §3.19 (2), (5); its far foot `B` beyond the land the METROPOLIS epoch's circuit encloses, so that circuit is laid across its deck;'. T-V6-47: 'a viaduct a later trace meets gets no gate' → 'its viaduct, which the METROPOLIS circuit meets, gets no gate on its deck, the main approach road's ground course taking that circuit's gate (gates counted on ground part 0)'.

claim: V06 §8's E3 row (l. 4231) lands T-V6-11 and T-V6-73 at E3's exit ('T-V6-9–11, 46–49, 57–61, 73'). Two of their clauses topple supports: T-V6-73's station's-regrowth clause, new this round from the END of VAP-r4-01 ('both spans beside the aqueduct's crossing station toppled'), and T-V6-11's second run ('a scripted `topple` of the support next to the station on either side'), now on H-AQUA's CITY ring. `topple` is an event-only hazard operator (V06 §3.11.4) that E5 builds ('… supports toppled and scoured …', l. 4233), so neither clause can run at E3's exit. T-V6-11's sky clause ('on a sky fixture whose island falls at year 30 …; exact on the landfall fixture') needs V05's P6 `fallIsland`, and M6-sky lands after M6-U while M6-E starts right after M4. INDEX §5 risk 2 and R5-05 (c) move such clauses to the first exit after the provider, each named in its volume; V06's cell names none. Nothing built changes.
required_change: V06 §8's E3 tests cell 'T-V6-9–11, 46–49, 57–61, 73' → 'T-V6-9–11, 46–49, 57–61, 73 (T-V6-11's runs on toppled supports and T-V6-73's station's regrowth at E5, which builds `topple`; T-V6-11's sky clause at the later of E3 and V05's P6, which builds the landfall)'.
